requests.detail: Priya Shah (Mumbai, POSH specialist) has the Internal Committee pack. External member consent is still unsigned, so nomination letters cannot be vaulted.
Faizan Qureshi is checking the Pune unit layout against DISH Maharashtra factory-licence thresholds — power, exits and worker count — before the application can move.

requirements.title: POSH implementation
requirements.description: Build the workplace prevention framework your organisation may need once employees are on the payroll.
requirements.applicability: Based on the information provided, this requirement may apply because your organisation has employees and operates in India. Verify with a qualified professional.

sources.title: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
sources.publisher: Ministry of Women and Child Development

steps.title: Understand applicability
steps.summary: Confirm whether the POSH framework is relevant to how you employ people today — not just whether a form exists.
steps.whyItMatters: If it applies and nothing is in place, employees have no clear path to raise a concern and the business has no defensible process.
steps.action: Review the applicability note against your headcount and workplace setup.

steps.title: Set up Internal Committee
steps.summary: Appoint members who can receive and examine complaints, including an external member as the law typically requires.
steps.whyItMatters: A policy without a committee is incomplete. People need to know who they can speak to.
steps.action: Nominate Internal Committee members and record their consent.

steps.title: Create / review policy
steps.summary: Write a plain-language policy that explains what is not acceptable, how to report, and what happens next.
steps.whyItMatters: Employees and managers cannot follow a process they cannot find or understand.
steps.action: Draft or review the POSH policy with professional support if needed.

steps.title: Employee awareness & training
steps.summary: Tell every employee that the policy exists, who is on the committee, and how to report a concern.
steps.whyItMatters: Awareness is part of the obligation, not an optional extra.
steps.action: Schedule a short awareness session and keep an attendance record.

steps.title: Ongoing compliance
steps.summary: Keep records, refresh training, and file any annual information the law may require.
steps.whyItMatters: POSH is not a one-time setup. It has to stay current as the team changes.
steps.action: Add annual review and filing reminders to your calendar.

requirements.title: GST filing
requirements.description: Stay current on GST returns for the Pune manufacturing operations.
requirements.applicability: Based on the information provided, GST return obligations may apply because the business is GST-registered. Verify filing positions with a GST practitioner.

sources.title: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 — return filing framework

steps.title: Confirm registration
steps.summary: Your GSTIN is on file. Keep the certificate accessible.
steps.whyItMatters: Buyers and officers will ask for the registration proof.
steps.action: Keep the GST certificate in the document vault.

steps.title: Prepare upcoming return
steps.summary: Collect invoices and reconcile outward and inward supplies for the period.
steps.whyItMatters: Late or mismatched returns attract notices and cash-flow surprises.
steps.action: Review the September filing pack.

steps.title: File and archive
steps.summary: File on GSTN and store acknowledgements with the period they belong to.
steps.whyItMatters: Proof of filing is needed during scrutiny or loan diligence.
steps.action: File with your CA or GST practitioner.

requirements.title: Shops & Establishment renewal
requirements.description: Renew the Pune establishment registration before it lapses.
requirements.applicability: A workplace in Maharashtra typically needs a shops or establishment registration. Confirm the exact local form with a licensing consultant.

sources.title: Maharashtra Shops and Establishments (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 2017

steps.title: Confirm Pune registration
steps.summary: Aarav Engineering already holds a Maharashtra Shops & Establishment certificate for the Pune unit.
steps.whyItMatters: Operating without a live registration can stop inspections, bank KYC and licence renewals further down the chain.
steps.action: Keep the establishment certificate in the vault and note the expiry.

steps.title: Assemble the renewal pack
steps.summary: Address proof, employer details and the existing certificate number sit together before the labour department asks for them.
steps.whyItMatters: Maharashtra renewals bounce when the address on the form does not match the unit.
steps.action: Collect address proof and match it to the Pune factory gate address.

steps.title: Review fee and Form A
steps.summary: Compute the renewal fee against current headcount (14) and check Form A particulars.
steps.whyItMatters: Wrong fee or an outdated occupier name is the usual reason a Mahakamgar filing sits in query.
steps.action: Review the renewal working papers before the 29 September window.

steps.title: File renewal on Mahakamgar
steps.summary: Submit the renewal on the Maharashtra labour portal and archive the acknowledgement against this certificate.
steps.whyItMatters: The next inspection and any Shop Act amendment start from this receipt.
steps.action: File inside SETU when the pack is signed off.

requirements.title: EPF monthly contribution
requirements.description: Deposit provident fund contributions for the current wage month.
requirements.applicability: With 14 employees, EPF coverage may already apply. Confirm establishment code and wage definitions with a CA or labour consultant.

sources.title: Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

steps.title: Confirm establishment code
steps.summary: Fourteen employees puts this unit inside EPF coverage. The establishment code must match EPFO records.
steps.whyItMatters: A wrong code files someone else's ECR, or none at all.
steps.action: Keep the PF establishment code next to the wage register.

steps.title: Prepare ECR from wages
steps.summary: Build the Electronic Challan cum Return from August / September wages for all 14 staff.
steps.whyItMatters: EPFO due date is the 15th. A late ECR is a late challan.
steps.action: Prepare the wage register and ECR working sheet.

steps.title: Generate challan
steps.summary: Once the ECR balances, generate the monthly challan for employer and employee share.
steps.whyItMatters: Payment without a matching ECR still shows as default on the unified portal.
steps.action: Raise the challan after Accounts signs the wage sheet.

steps.title: File on EPFO unified portal
steps.summary: Submit ECR and pay the challan on the unified portal, then drop the TRRN into the vault.
steps.whyItMatters: TRRN is the only proof a lender or inspector will accept.
steps.action: File inside SETU on or before 15 September.

requirements.title: ESI coverage check
requirements.description: Confirm whether ESI applies to current wage bands at the Pune unit.
requirements.applicability: ESI may apply depending on wage limits and location. This is a check, not a conclusion.

steps.title: Check wage-band coverage
steps.summary: ESI applies only where wages sit under the notified ceiling and the unit is in a notified area. Pune is notified; the wage bands still need a pass.
steps.whyItMatters: Registering people who are out of coverage, or missing people who are in, both attract ESIC notices.
steps.action: Review the September wage register against the current ESI wage limit.

steps.title: Confirm ESIC code
steps.summary: If any employee is covered, the employer code on the ESIC portal must already exist for this Pune unit.
steps.whyItMatters: Contribution cannot be filed against a code that does not match the factory address.
steps.action: Confirm whether Aarav already has an ESIC employer code.

steps.title: Prepare monthly contribution
steps.summary: Split employer and employee share for covered staff only.
steps.whyItMatters: A blended wage sheet that includes excluded staff will not match the ESIC challan.
steps.action: Draft the contribution statement from the wage register.

steps.title: File on ESIC employer portal
steps.summary: Pay and file the monthly return, then store the ESIC acknowledgement.
steps.whyItMatters: Medical benefit for staff, and inspection defence, both start from this receipt.
steps.action: File inside SETU once coverage is confirmed.

requirements.title: MCA annual filings
requirements.description: AOC-4 and MGT-7 remain on the annual calendar for a private limited company.
requirements.applicability: Private limited companies typically file annual financial and ownership returns with MCA.

steps.title: Close the books
steps.summary: FY books for the Pune company are with the CA. Trial balance is in a shape a CS can file from.
steps.whyItMatters: AOC-4 cannot be filed on draft numbers that still move.
steps.action: Keep the closed books pack together.

steps.title: Director KYC current
steps.summary: DIR-3 KYC for the sitting directors is already marked current for this year.
steps.whyItMatters: MCA blocks annual filing if a director KYC is overdue.
steps.action: No further KYC this week.

steps.title: Draft AOC-4
steps.summary: Financial statements and Board report mapped into AOC-4 working papers.
steps.whyItMatters: Wrong auditor or attachment set is the usual SRN rejection.
steps.action: Leave the AOC-4 draft with the CS.

steps.title: Draft MGT-7
steps.summary: Annual return — shareholding, directors, and registered office — still needs a last pass before MCA21.
steps.whyItMatters: MGT-7 is the ownership picture. A mismatch with the register is a compounding event.
steps.action: Keep books ready for the CS review of MGT-7.

steps.title: File AOC-4 and MGT-7
steps.summary: Upload on MCA21, pay the fee, and vault the SRNs against this company.
steps.whyItMatters: Private limited companies stay visible to lenders and MCA only while these two returns are current.
steps.action: File on MCA21 before 30 November.

requirements.title: Factory licence validity
requirements.description: Manufacturing premises may need a factory licence depending on power and worker count.
requirements.applicability: Based on engineering/manufacturing activity, a factory licence may apply. Confirm thresholds with the state inspectorate.

sources.title: Factories Act, 1948 — licensing and safety
sources.publisher: Maharashtra Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health

steps.title: Test Factories Act coverage
steps.summary: Pune unit does engineering / manufacturing with power. That usually pulls the premises into the Factories Act, not only Shop Act.
steps.whyItMatters: A shop registration does not cover a powered manufacturing floor.
steps.action: Treat factory licensing as in scope until DISH says otherwise.

steps.title: Collect approved layout
steps.summary: DISH wants a layout that shows machinery, exits, welfare rooms and the occupied area.
steps.whyItMatters: Applications without a scaled layout are returned. This is where the file is stuck.
steps.action: Wait for the licensing consultant to mark the Pune layout against DISH norms.

steps.title: Attach power sanction
steps.summary: Connected load from MSEDCL (or the current sanction letter) has to match the layout's machinery list.
steps.whyItMatters: Licence category follows horsepower. A mismatch is a query, not a licence.
steps.action: Pull the power sanction once the layout is accepted.

steps.title: Safety and welfare checklist
steps.summary: Toilets, drinking water, first aid and fencing as the Factories Act expects for this headcount.
steps.whyItMatters: DISH inspects what the layout promised.
steps.action: Walk the shop floor against the layout.

steps.title: Apply / renew with DISH
steps.summary: File the factory licence (or renewal) on the Maharashtra DISH portal and vault the licence copy.
steps.whyItMatters: Running a powered factory without this licence is a prosecutable default.
steps.action: File inside SETU after layout and power papers are in.

requirements.title: Professional tax
requirements.description: Maharashtra professional tax for employees is currently on track.
requirements.applicability: Employers in Maharashtra typically deduct and remit professional tax.

sources.title: Maharashtra Shops and Establishments (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 2017

steps.title: PT enrolment on file
steps.summary: Maharashtra professional tax enrolment for the Pune employer is already in the register.
steps.whyItMatters: You cannot remit PT against a lapsed enrolment.
steps.action: Keep the PT registration certificate in the vault.

steps.title: Deduct from payroll
steps.summary: Slab-wise PT is already deducted for all 14 employees on the current payroll run.
steps.whyItMatters: Under-deduction is recovered from the employer, not the staff.
steps.action: No payroll change this week.

steps.title: Prepare the monthly return
steps.summary: Employee-wise deduction list matches the PT portal template.
steps.whyItMatters: A return that does not match challan amount is the usual PT notice.
steps.action: Keep the working paper with Accounts.

steps.title: Remit on the PT portal
steps.summary: Pay September professional tax and archive the MHPT acknowledgement.
steps.whyItMatters: Maharashtra PT is a monthly rhythm. Missing one month is a compounding late fee.
steps.action: Remit before 30 September. No action this week unless payroll changes.

glossary.plain: Your 15-digit GST number — the tax identity of the business.
The receipt number you get after a GST filing goes through.
The monthly PF contribution sheet you send to EPFO.
The workplace law that requires a policy and a complaints committee once you have employees.
The group of people employees can go to with a POSH complaint.
The yearly MCA form that files your company accounts.
The receipt number EPFO gives you after a PF payment.
The monthly (or quarterly) GST summary return.
Employee State Insurance — medical cover funded by a small payroll deduction.
The ministry that keeps company records. Filings go through MCA21.

penalties.label: Workplace policy gap
penalties.consequence: Fine and possible cancellation of a business licence if a complaint arrives with no committee in place.
penalties.sourceNote: POSH Act, 2013 — illustrative band for the demo, not a citation of a live case.

penalties.label: Late GSTR-3B
penalties.consequence: Late fee plus interest on unpaid tax. The return stays blocked until the fee is cleared.
penalties.sourceNote: CGST Rules — late fee is typically ₹50/day per Act, capped. Demo uses a round number.

penalties.label: Delayed PF contribution
penalties.consequence: Damages on the delayed amount plus possible prosecution for repeated default.
penalties.sourceNote: EPF & MP Act — damages are percentage-banded. Demo uses a mid-band figure.

penalties.label: Expired Shop Act registration
penalties.consequence: Local inspector can issue a notice; renewal often needs a late fee.
penalties.sourceNote: Maharashtra Shops and Establishments Act — municipal bands vary.

penalties.label: Missed annual MCA filing
penalties.consequence: Additional fee that grows with delay; directors can be marked as disqualified.
penalties.sourceNote: Companies Act additional-fee table — demo uses a rounded exposure.

penalties.label: ESI contribution slip
penalties.consequence: Interest and damages on delayed contribution, plus recovery action.

penalties.label: Factory licence lapse
penalties.consequence: Running a factory without a valid licence can attract a notice to stop work.
penalties.sourceNote: Factories Act / DISH Maharashtra — demo band.

penalties.label: Professional tax delay
penalties.consequence: Interest on unpaid tax and a small penalty per employee.
